questions.question: Which famous ancient statue is this?
questions.explanation: The Sphinx has a lion's body and a king's head, and was carved straight out of the rock of the Giza plateau.

media.alt: A huge stone statue in the desert with a pyramid behind it

questions.question: Which young pharaoh's golden mask is this?
questions.explanation: Howard Carter found his tomb in 1922, and the mask contains more than 10 kilograms of gold.

media.alt: A gleaming gold and blue striped mask

questions.question: Which ancient monument is this?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

media.alt: A huge stone pyramid in the desert
media.credit: Photo: Douwe C. van der Zee, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which famous Roman building is this?
questions.explanation: The Pantheon's dome is nearly 1,900 years old and is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.

media.alt: An ancient building with a columned porch

questions.question: What were the Vikings' long, narrow wooden ships called?
questions.explanation: Their shallow hulls let Vikings sail far up rivers as well as across the open sea.

questions.question: Which river was the lifeline of ancient Egypt?
questions.explanation: Every summer the Nile flooded and left behind rich black mud, perfect for growing crops.

questions.question: What did the ancient Egyptians write on, made from a reed that grew by the river?
questions.explanation: Our word paper comes from papyrus.

questions.question: What do we call the picture writing used in ancient Egypt?
questions.explanation: For centuries nobody could read them, until the Rosetta Stone helped crack the code in the 1820s.

questions.question: Which Roman emperor ordered a wall to be built right across northern England?
questions.explanation: Hadrian's Wall ran for about 73 miles, from coast to coast.

questions.question: Where were the first Olympic Games held, in ancient Greece?
questions.explanation: The first games are traditionally dated to 776 BC, and winners were crowned with olive leaves.

questions.question: What were ancient Egyptian mummies wrapped in?
questions.explanation: Lucky charms called amulets were often tucked in between the layers of linen.

questions.question: What did the Romans call Britain?
questions.explanation: Britannia later became the helmeted figure who has appeared on British coins for centuries.

questions.question: Which English city did the Vikings call Jorvik?
questions.explanation: Archaeologists in York have dug up Viking houses, leather shoes and even a 20-centimetre lump of fossilised Viking poo.

questions.question: Which hard stone did Stone Age people chip into sharp tools and arrowheads?
questions.explanation: Flint breaks with edges sharp enough to cut meat and scrape animal skins.

questions.question: What was a Roman army officer in charge of around 80 soldiers called?
questions.explanation: Despite the name, which comes from the Latin for a hundred, a centurion's unit usually had about 80 men.

questions.question: Which famous ancient object is this?
questions.explanation: It carries the same decree in hieroglyphs, Demotic and ancient Greek, which is what let scholars finally read hieroglyphs.

media.alt: A dark slab of stone covered in carved writing
media.credit: Photo: Hans Hillewaert, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which ancient temple is this?
options: The Temple of Poseidon at Sounion
questions.explanation: It was built in the 5th century BC for Athena, the patron goddess of Athens.

media.alt: A ruined marble temple with columns on top of a hill
media.credit: Photo: Steve Swayne, CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which queen of the Iceni led a great revolt against the Romans in Britain?
questions.explanation: Her army burned the Roman towns at Colchester, London and St Albans.

questions.question: Which emperor was ruling Rome when much of the city burned in AD 64?
questions.explanation: The story that he fiddled while Rome burned cannot be true: the fiddle had not been invented yet.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek city-state took boys away from home at the age of seven to train as soldiers?
questions.explanation: The tough Spartan training was called the agoge, and it lasted well into a boy's teens.

questions.question: Which pharaoh was the Great Pyramid of Giza built for?
questions.explanation: For more than 3,800 years it was the tallest structure ever built by people.

questions.question: What did the Romans call their town of London?
questions.explanation: The Romans founded it within a few years of their invasion in AD 43 and built the first London Bridge.

questions.question: Which Greek philosopher was tutor to the young Alexander the Great?
questions.explanation: Aristotle had studied under Plato, who had himself been a pupil of Socrates.

questions.question: Which Carthaginian general crossed the Alps with war elephants to attack Rome?
questions.explanation: He made the crossing in 218 BC, though few of his elephants survived for long in Italy.

questions.question: Which Viking explorer is said in the sagas to have reached North America around the year 1000?
questions.explanation: Norse remains at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland, with wood cut in 1021, prove Vikings reached the Americas almost 500 years before Columbus.

questions.question: Whose tomb do these clay figures guard?
questions.explanation: Farmers digging a well near Xi'an stumbled on the first figures in 1974.

media.alt: Rows of life-size clay figures standing in a pit

questions.question: In which country is this Roman aqueduct bridge?
questions.explanation: The Pont du Gard was built in the 1st century AD to carry water to the city of Nîmes.

media.alt: A three-tiered stone bridge of arches over a river
media.credit: Photo: Benh LIEU SONG (Flickr), CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which Roman town was buried by Vesuvius in AD 79 along with Pompeii?
questions.explanation: Herculaneum lay under about 20 metres of volcanic material, which preserved wooden beams and furniture.

questions.question: In which year did Vikings raid the monastery on Lindisfarne, often seen as the start of the Viking Age in Britain?
questions.explanation: The attack on Holy Island, off the Northumberland coast, shocked the whole of Christian Europe.

questions.question: Which Stone Age village in Orkney was uncovered when a great storm stripped away the sand in 1850?
questions.explanation: Its houses still have their stone beds and dressers, and the village is older than the Great Pyramid.
